questions.prompt: Match each API to its job in a presentational component.

pairs.right: Data the component can't work without
Reports a user action to the parent
Re-checks only when inputs, events, or read signals change

questions.explanation: Presentational components take essential data through required inputs, report intents through outputs, derive display values with computed(), and use OnPush for cheap change detection.

questions.prompt: An EntryItem has a '+1 rep' button. What should its click handler do?

options.text: Inject the diary service and save the new value
Emit a new object like { ...entry, reps: entry.reps + 1 } and let the parent apply it
Call the parent component directly through viewChild()

questions.explanation: The entry belongs to the parent. The child describes the change with an output, and the owner updates its state immutably.

questions.prompt: Why might this fail to update the view: entries.update(list => { list.push(x); return list; })?

options.text: update() only works with primitive values
It returns the same array reference, so the signal sees no change
push() is not allowed in TypeScript strict mode

questions.explanation: Signals compare values with Object.is. Returning the same reference looks like 'no change'. Return a new array such as [...list, x].

questions.prompt: Put the steps of unidirectional data flow in order, starting from a user clicking Delete.

items.text: The presentational item emits remove with the entry id
The presentational list re-emits the event
The smart page calls the service and filters its entries signal into a new array
The new array flows back down through inputs and the view updates

questions.explanation: Events travel up to the single owner of the state, which updates it, and the new state flows back down.

questions.prompt: Which are signs you should move state into a shared service instead of bubbling events? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Inputs pass through several components that don't use them
Unrelated parts of the page need the same state
A parent and its direct child share one value
You re-emit the same output through four or five layers

questions.explanation: Prop drilling and state shared by unrelated components call for a service. A direct parent-child relationship is exactly what inputs and outputs are for.

questions.prompt: In a unit test, which method on fixture.componentRef sets a signal input?
questions.explanation: fixture.componentRef.setInput('entries', value) sets the input, then fixture.detectChanges() renders it.
